summary.text: Tim Turner is a Republican who was elected in 2024 to represent Oklahoma House District 15, which includes parts of Haskell, Le Flore, McIntosh, Muskogee and Pittsburg counties. He is a lifelong resident of the district and a former Haskell County sheriff.

paragraphs.text: Turner began his career as a 911 dispatcher in Checotah and later served as Haskell County sheriff and in other law enforcement roles.

He was a district attorney’s taskforce officer with the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration and was appointed in 2022 by Gov. Stitt to the Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation Commission, a post he resigned upon taking state office.
His awards include Oklahoma Sheriff of the Year and the Medal of Valor from the Oklahoma Sheriffs Association.
Turner and his wife, Brooke, live in Kinta with their son, Sawyer, and are members of Stigler First Assembly.
He is president of the Haskell County Livestock Committee and coaches Little League football.
